description: The environmental contaminant 2,3,7,8-tetrachlorodibenzo-p-dioxin (TCDD) binds the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR), which is held in the cytoplasm by HSP90 and the co-chaperone AIP. Ligand binding releases the receptor, which moves to the nucleus, dimerises with ARNT and induces the xenobiotic-metabolising enzymes CYP1A1, CYP1B1 and NQO1 and the repressor AHRR in human cells.
title: Aryl hydrocarbon receptor activation by dioxin
